newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS- SM Investments shops for funds.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS- SM Investments shops for funds.

text.p: A US$100 million floating rate note issue for the Philippines SM Investments was formally launched into Asian debt markets on Friday.
The notes were launched via special purpose vehicle SM International and guaranteed by SM Investments, which is the holding company parent of shopping mall developer SM Prime.

The 5-1/2 year notes were priced at par to float at 100 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate. Fees are a flat 30 basis points for an all-in return of roughly 105.5 basis points. Merrill Lynch Far East and LTCB Asia are the joint lead managers. Merrill handled the books.
The issue was launched bond style on Friday but the term sheet has been circulating for a while and a group had already formed by the time of the formal launch.
Merrill Lynch kept US$17.5 million and LTCB Asia held onto US$17 million. Fourteen other banks split the remainder.
Bankers complained that the pricing was tight, while conceding that outstanding paper of the SM group had performed well in the secondary market over the last several months.

Philippines credits received a boost when Standard and Poor's Corp upgraded the country's sovereign rating to BB-plus in February and have remained well supported despite volatility in emerging markets since then.
SM Prime launched a 5-1/2 year bond last August that was priced to yield 200 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries. Fees were 75 basis points.
Since then, the bond has tightened considerably to trade at around 135-145 basis points over the benchmark.
On a swap basis, that translates into about 110-120 basis points over LIBOR.
"We still think the deal is tight and that the unit SM Prime, which is an operating company, is a better credit than the parent," one trader said.
A number of other Philippine issues are in the pipeline, bankers said.
Metrobank is expected to launch its US$150 million issue next week via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. Rizal Commercial Bank is taking proposals for three- or five-year paper, bankers said.
Among corporate issuers, bankers said Benpres is eyeing a Eurobond, while real estate company Filinvest Development Corp plans a floating rate note issue.
In the loan market, Indian Oil Corp plans to raise US$1.0 billion through one-year syndicated loan facilities, according to an Indian newspaper.
It said ABN Amro Bank, Kredietbank NV and Dresdner South-East Asia will arrange the loans.
BII Finance Co launched a US$30 million transferable loan facility via KMBC Asia and Standard Chartered Bank.
BII Finance is registered as a deposit-taking company in Hong Kong and is wholly owned by Bank Internasional Indonesia.
Bankers said a US$58 million term loan facility for Industrial and Commercial Bank of China now is in general syndication. BA Asia is the mandated arranger, they said.
Apart from the Hong Kong dollar issues, debt issuance was thin this week and bankers do not foresee much increase in activity next week.
Pakistan will start roadshowing its floating rate note issue in Singapore on Monday. ANZ is lead manager.
India's Sterlite Industries US$70 million FRN will be presented to Hong Kong investors on Tuesday by lead manager UBS.
